title: Suspension trauma and rescue planning
audience: Workers, supervisors and designated rescuers on any job where an arrest system may be used.
learningOutcomes: Recognise the early signs of suspension trauma and the response each one needs.
Name the components a rescue plan must cover before any arrest system is used.
Describe the categories of rescue named in the sources and the conditions under which each applies.
State the stop-work condition where no safe rescue arrangement exists.

instruction.heading: A harness can save a life and still injure
instruction.body: A worker held in a harness after a fall can be injured by the arrest itself, and can become unconscious while still suspended. The sources describe a condition often called suspension trauma. It can follow when a person hangs motionless, with circulation affected in the legs, and the person may faint. One source gives time markers for fainting and for death. The response does not depend on the exact timing. The rescue must be fast, and the plan must exist before the work starts.

instruction.heading: Early signs and first response
instruction.body: Watch for the early warning signs: a rush of light-headedness or nausea, a flushed or tingling feeling, numbness, faintness or anxiety; treat any of them as a warning. A suspended worker who is unconscious needs rescue as soon as it can be done safely. If a rescue cannot be started straight away, the sources suggest moving the legs or supporting the feet, and raising the lower legs where that can be done, to ease the strain. That response buys time. It is not the rescue, and it must not replace the rescue plan. Medical help is still needed after the rescue, whatever the apparent severity.

instruction.heading: What a rescue plan must cover
instruction.body: Before any arrest system is used, the plan must name who will rescue, which rescue method will be used, where the rescue equipment is kept, how the rescuer will reach the worker, and how emergency services will be called. One source says that a rescue plan which has not been practised cannot be depended on. Where the existing rescue method is not judged safe enough, the work does not start until a safe method is found. Work in teams: a lone worker cannot be rescued in time, and the sources prohibit lone working at height where fall arrest is used.

instruction.heading: Four categories of rescue
instruction.body: The sources sort rescues into four kinds: getting a casualty down from a distance, hauling a casualty up from a distance, the worker descending under their own power, and helping a second person who is on the way down. A rescuer should avoid descending or being suspended to reach someone else where that can be avoided, because it can create a second casualty. The sources name methods that include a rescue ladder, pulling a person in through a window or balcony, pulling a person up through an opening, lowering, climbing or descending the structure, an elevated platform, and a crane basket. The method is chosen to fit the location and the risk assessment.

instruction.heading: Rescue using an elevating platform
instruction.body: Where a platform can reach the suspended worker, an operator trained for that platform positions it beneath the worker. The platform's capacity must cover both the worker and the rescuer. An unconscious worker may need two rescuers to move them into the platform. The lanyard is disconnected only once the worker is secure in the platform, and reconnected to a platform anchor where possible. The worker is then lowered and given first aid.

instruction.heading: Raising and lowering a worker
instruction.body: Raising a worker needs two or more capable people hauling on a second line, with the slack taken up so that the rope does not slip. Lowering needs a rescuer anchored to a strong point, and someone at the bottom to guide the descent. In both cases, first aid and treatment for suspension trauma as well as for other injuries follow once the worker is safe.

instruction.heading: After the rescue
instruction.body: Do not let the worker stand straight away after a rescue. The sources advise against it and call for medical assessment, even where the worker seems well. Take the worker for examination at a medical facility. Report the fall to the supervisor and to the business's escalation contact. The equipment that was in use is withdrawn and recorded under “Inspecting and fitting harnesses and lanyards”.

procedure: Before work starts, confirm a named rescuer, a rescue method, and the rescue equipment at the work location.
Confirm the emergency contact and that the route for calling it is clear.
Brief everyone involved on the plan and on their role in it.
If no safe rescue is available, stop. Do not start fall-arrest work.
On any fall, a trained person checks the worker and starts the rescue while the emergency services are called.
Start the chosen rescue method, and keep the rescuer protected from falling.
On reaching the worker, check responsiveness and breathing, and manage suspension trauma while the rescue continues.
After the rescue, keep the worker still, arrange medical assessment, and report the event.

workedExamples.situation: A two-person crew sets up a roof anchor for a harness. The only rescue arrangement written down is to call an ambulance.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Calling an ambulance is one part of the plan, but the rescue itself must happen quickly, and the plan must name who rescues, with what equipment and by which method. Stop, set the rescue method, and confirm the people and equipment before anyone is attached to the anchor.

workedExamples.situation: A glazing contractor's rescue plan has been written, but the rescue kit is in the van about 200 metres away from the work.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the plan need before the worker goes up?
workedExamples.reasoning: The rescue equipment must be at the work location before the work starts. The kit is moved to the work location, its readiness is checked, and the worker does not go up until that is recorded.

equipmentAndPpe: Rescue kit or rescue equipment at the work location
Harness with a rescue or descent option
Phone or radio, and a written call-out sheet
First-aid kit suited to the job

commonErrors.error: Writing a rescue plan that is never practised.
commonErrors.prevention: Practise the chosen method with the team before first use, and record the practice.

commonErrors.error: Working alone at height with an arrest system.
commonErrors.prevention: Work with a trained rescuer present.

commonErrors.error: Sending a rescuer into a dangerous position without protection.
commonErrors.prevention: The rescuer is protected from falling, and avoids being suspended where that can be avoided.

commonErrors.error: Letting a suspended worker stay still for a long time.
commonErrors.prevention: Start the rescue at once, and move the legs or support the feet while waiting.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Warning: an unconscious or motionless suspended worker needs rescue as soon as it can be done safely. Do not wait for emergency services before starting the rescue.
Warning: if there is no safe rescue arrangement, fall-arrest work does not start.
The rescue must be fast whatever the exact figures.
Rescue methods and equipment are not taught by this lesson.

Licence notice: completing this lesson does not grant rescue competence, a licence, or authority to operate an elevating platform for rescue. Rope access and specialist rescue are outside this course (see “Rope access and anchor certification”).

qualityStandard: A rescue plan has been written before work starts, with named people, a method and equipment.
The rescue kit is confirmed at the work location.
The suspension response steps are known to everyone on the job.
documentationEvidence: Rescue plan with the named rescuer and method
Incident and first-aid record after any rescue
summary: A suspended worker needs rescue at once, not at a convenient time.
No fall-arrest work starts without a rescue plan that names people, method and equipment.
Practise the method. A plan that has never been practised is not reliable.
After any rescue, the worker is medically assessed, even if they seem well.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which is the sound response when a worker is suspended and cannot move?
options: Leave the worker while waiting for a convenient time today
Start the rescue at once with the planned method, and check the worker.
Tell the worker to hang still until help arrives and do nothing else
Let the worker stand as soon as they feel dizzy and walk around

knowledgeChecks.question: What has to exist before an arrest system is used?
options: A rescue plan that names the rescuer, the method and the equipment at the work location.
A sign at the base of the ladder and a note on the wall of the room and a second sign
An approved colour for the harness and a label on the strap and a spare
A written statement that the worker is experienced and a copy of their certificate

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a rescuer avoid being suspended when helping another person?
options: Because suspended rescuers cannot speak and cannot see the worker below
Because it can create a second casualty and complicate the rescue.
Because harnesses are not allowed for rescuers in any case
Because rescuers must stand on the harness to lift faster.
